checkpoints.description: [1/6] Plan: M1 catalog v4 (copies per person, profile folder, password hash, sessions) + store writes readable paths <Person>/<YYYY>/<YYYY-MM>/ with hard-linked shared photos; M2 resumable reorganiser moving existing files + library README.txt + hidden .harbor + folder rename; M3 accounts: PBKDF2 passwords, sessions, name+password login (key fallback), change/reset password, login rate limit, per-person privacy on every endpoint; M4 UI: login picker, My account, owner resets, window Open folder + set password, disk-space warning; M5 weekly integrity check; M6 tests, docs, ADR-007/008, review, screenshots

impact_assessment.why: User asked that each person reach their own photos, change their passwords, and find photos in plain, understandable Windows folders usable without Harbor; plus proposals 1 and 3
impact_assessment.benefits: Private per-person galleries, password sign-in, photos browsable in File Explorer, early warning before the disk fills or a file rots
impact_assessment.risks: contract: login moves from keys to name+password, non-owners lose the everyone view, on-disk layout changes; dependency: none new (hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac, os.link); concurrency: reorganiser moving files while uploads arrive; state: catalog v3->v4 migration and moving every original
impact_assessment.mitigation: Key sign-in kept as fallback; migration additive with backup copy; file moves are per-file, resumable, verified by size, done under the store's placement lock; hard link falls back to copy
